ideas.name: Allowance Gap Agent
ideas.what_it_does: Prices the emission allowances each European voyage needs and shows where the surcharge falls short, loop by loop.
room: Pick a Europe loop and a month
The agent prices the allowances each voyage needs
It sets the cost per container beside today's surcharge
It proposes next month's surcharge and drafts the customer notice

how.spot: Finds the voyages to and from EU ports in the published schedule
how.check: Checks each port pair against the rules for voyages inside and into or out of the EU
how.calculate: Works out the allowances per voyage and the cost per container
how.propose: Proposes a surcharge that closes the gap, with its basis
how.prepare: Drafts the monthly surcharge notice for customers
how.decision: Pricing approves or changes the surcharge before it goes out

key_figures.name: Extra cost recovered through surcharges
key_figures.demo: Rises loop by loop as the proposed surcharge closes the gap

key_figures.name: Money at stake a year
key_figures.demo: The uncovered allowance cost across Europe services, {{fact:issue.bmc-I1.eur}} a year

data: Published sailing schedules and port calls
risks: Allowance prices change daily, so the demo fixes a date
Emissions per ship are estimates until the company shares its own

value.reason: The uncovered cost per container is easy to grasp

evidence.reason: The rules and prices are public; the company's volumes are not

buildable.reason: Schedules and prices are public, volumes can be synthetic

agentic.reason: It checks each voyage, prices it and asks pricing to decide

relevance.reason: All three challengers raised this cost

demo.reason: One loop shows the gap and the fix in minutes

risk.reason: Surcharges are touchy with large customers

ideas.why: It turns the cost all three challengers raised into a surcharge decision the room can follow.

ideas.name: FuelEU Pool Planner
ideas.what_it_does: Finds the ships above the FuelEU Maritime limit and proposes pools with cleaner ships that avoid the penalty.
room: The fleet appears with each ship's fuel and intensity
The agent marks the ships above the limit
It proposes pools with the dual-fuel newbuilds
It shows the penalty with and without each pool

how.spot: Finds the ships whose energy use is above the limit for the year
how.check: Checks which cleaner ships have room to cover them
how.calculate: Works out the penalty each ship would pay alone and in a pool
how.propose: Proposes the pools that remove the most penalty
how.prepare: Prepares the pooling summary for the verifier
how.decision: The fleet manager chooses which pools to register

key_figures.name: Emissions per container kilometre
key_figures.demo: Falls for the pooled fleet against the limit

key_figures.name: Money saved a year
key_figures.demo: The penalty avoided, against {{fact:issue.pestel-I2.eur}} at stake

data: The FuelEU Maritime limits and penalty rules
risks: Pooling rules leave room for interpretation
Fuel use per ship is synthetic

value.reason: A penalty avoided is a clear sum

evidence.reason: The limits and penalties are published

buildable.reason: Rules are public; ship data must be synthetic

agentic.reason: It weighs many pool options and asks a person to choose

relevance.reason: The older ships still burn heavy fuel oil

demo.reason: Pooling takes a minute to explain

risk.reason: Compliance figures need a verifier's check

ideas.why: It shows a penalty shrink as the agent pairs old ships with new ones.

ideas.name: Route Risk Desk
ideas.what_it_does: Weighs each Asia loop's route every week from security notices, war-risk cost and fuel, and proposes the route.
room: This week's security notices come in
The agent sets the Suez and Cape routes side by side for one loop
It prices fuel, war-risk cover and days at sea
It proposes a route and drafts the customer advisory

how.spot: Spots notices that change the risk on a route
how.check: Checks them against the loop's next sailings
how.calculate: Prices each route in fuel, cover and days
how.propose: Proposes the route for the next sailing
how.prepare: Drafts the advisory to customers on the loop
how.decision: The network planner confirms or overrides the route

key_figures.name: Schedule reliability
key_figures.demo: Holds as routes change ahead of trouble

key_figures.name: Detection to decision
key_figures.demo: Drops from a weekly meeting to the same day

risks: Security news is sensitive and changes fast

value.reason: Rerouting puts the most money at stake of all issues

evidence.reason: The route closures and returns are well reported

agentic.reason: It reads news, prices options and hands a person the call

relevance.reason: It is this year's largest pain

demo.reason: Two routes on a map make the choice obvious

risk.reason: War and security make it politically sensitive

ideas.why: It shows an agent turning the week's news into a priced route choice.

ideas.name: Rate Index Watch
ideas.what_it_does: Compares contract rates with the weekly freight index and proposes which contracts to reprice or index-link.
room: The weekly index lands
The agent compares it with each contract's rate
It ranks the contracts by margin at risk
It drafts an index clause for the top account

how.spot: Spots contracts whose rate has drifted from the index
how.check: Checks each contract's repricing date and volume
how.calculate: Works out the margin at risk until the next repricing
how.propose: Proposes which contracts to reprice or link to the index
how.prepare: Drafts the index clause and a note for the account manager
how.decision: The commercial lead decides which offers go out

key_figures.name: Average freight rate
key_figures.demo: Contract rates follow the index with a lag the agent closes

value.reason: Margin at risk per contract is easy to follow

evidence.reason: The index is published every week

buildable.reason: Only the contract book must be synthetic

agentic.reason: It checks each contract and asks before offers go out

relevance.reason: Rate swings hit margins every quarter

risk.reason: Pricing talk with customers needs care

ideas.why: It ties a public index the room knows to a decision on real contracts.

ideas.name: Instant Spot Quote
ideas.what_it_does: Answers a small shipper's spot booking request with a checked quote in minutes instead of a working day.
room: A booking request arrives by e-mail
The agent reads it and checks space on the loop
It prices the quote with surcharges
It drafts the reply for an agent to send

how.spot: Picks out the route, dates and cargo from the request
how.check: Checks space and cut-off times on the loop
how.calculate: Prices the quote with every surcharge
how.propose: Proposes the quote and an alternative sailing
how.prepare: Drafts the reply in the shipper's language
how.decision: A customer service agent sends, edits or rejects it

key_figures.name: Booking response time
key_figures.demo: Falls from a working day to minutes

key_figures.name: People affected
key_figures.demo: The small shippers who get an answer the same hour

risks: A wrong quote binds the company

value.reason: The lost bookings are hard to price

evidence.reason: Response times are the company's own and not published

buildable.reason: Requests and schedules are easy to simulate

agentic.reason: It checks space and prices before a person sends

relevance.reason: Digital forwarders take small shippers now

demo.reason: A request answered live lands at once

ideas.why: Everyone in the room has waited for a quote, and here it comes in minutes.

ideas.name: Emissions per Box
ideas.what_it_does: Writes an emissions statement per container to the EN ISO 14083 method and attaches it to every bill of lading.
room: A shipper asks for the emissions of a shipment
The agent finds the voyage legs and the ship
It works out the emissions per container
It drafts the statement for the bill of lading

how.spot: Spots shipments whose customers ask for emissions data
how.check: Checks the legs, the ship and the cargo against the method
how.calculate: Works out the emissions per container and leg
how.propose: Proposes the statement with its assumptions
how.prepare: Prepares it for the bill of lading
how.decision: Sustainability signs off the method once, sales sends each statement

key_figures.name: Emissions per container kilometre
key_figures.demo: Shown per shipment instead of a yearly average

key_figures.name: Money at stake a year
key_figures.demo: The tender volume at risk, {{fact:issue.bmc-I3.eur}} a year

risks: Emission factors per ship are estimates
Customers may compare figures across carriers

value.reason: Tenders lost without the data are easy to see

evidence.reason: The method and the counting rules are public

buildable.reason: Ship data is public, shipments synthetic

agentic.reason: Much of it is a fixed calculation

relevance.reason: Shippers ask for it in tenders now

demo.reason: A statement per container is concrete

risk.reason: Figures will be compared and challenged

ideas.why: It answers what shippers now ask in every tender, per container.

ideas.name: Empty Moves Planner
ideas.what_it_does: Forecasts where empty containers pile up and proposes the repositioning moves for the coming week.
room: The depots appear with their stock of empties
The agent forecasts demand by port
It proposes the moves for the week
It drafts the instructions to the depots

how.spot: Spots depots heading for too many or too few empties
how.check: Checks the sailings that can carry them
how.calculate: Works out the cost of each move and of waiting
how.decision: The equipment controller approves the moves

key_figures.name: Empty container moves
key_figures.demo: Falls as moves follow the forecast

key_figures.name: Dwell time
key_figures.demo: Shortens in the North European depots

risks: The forecast rests on synthetic data

value.reason: Moves saved are easy to price

evidence.reason: Depot data is the company's own

agentic.reason: It plans moves and asks before they happen

relevance.reason: A known weakness, not this year's main pain

demo.reason: A map of depots needs some explaining

ideas.why: It shows planning by forecast where judgement rules today.

ideas.name: Invoice Explainer
ideas.what_it_does: Spots surcharge lines customers are likely to dispute and explains each one on the invoice before it goes out.
room: An invoice with an emissions surcharge comes up
The agent spots the lines that drew disputes before
It writes a plain explanation for each
It adds the explanation and flags the invoice for review

how.spot: Spots surcharge lines like those disputed before
how.check: Checks each line against the published surcharge
how.calculate: Works out how the line was priced
how.prepare: Prepares the invoice with the explanation

key_figures.name: Invoice accuracy
key_figures.demo: Rises as disputed lines get explained first

key_figures.name: Lead time
key_figures.demo: Payment arrives sooner without a dispute

risks: Dispute history is the company's own

value.reason: Faster payment is clear, but no sum is stated

relevance.reason: It follows from the new surcharge

demo.reason: An invoice explained line by line is easy to follow

ideas.why: It keeps the new surcharge from slowing payment.
